rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The register of deeds contains every deed, from the weightiest to the tiniest, and preserves both small and great actions.
rows.anchor: كتاب الأعمال، الذي فيه الجليل والحقير، والفتيل والقطمير، والصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers fear the record because it contains their evil acts; their cry of woe laments what they squandered of their lives.
rows.anchor: فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه} أي: من أعمالهم السيئة وأفعالهم القبيحة، {ويقولون يا ويلتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book omits no sin, great or small, nor any deed however slight; it has counted and preserved them.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يترك ذنبا صغيرا ولا كبيرا ولا عملا وإن صغر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After Hunayn the Prophet compared a heap made from gathered sticks to sins accumulating on a person and warned everyone to avoid even small sins because they are recorded; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: إلى سعد ابن جنادة قال: لما فرغ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من غزوة حنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will find every good or evil deed present, and hidden thoughts exposed; he links this to 3:30, 75:13, and 86:9.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا} أي: من خير أوشر كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that every treacherous person will be identified on Judgment Day by a banner marking his betrayal; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لكل غادر لواء يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God judges all deeds without wronging anyone; by power, wisdom, and justice He pardons or punishes, rescues sinful believers from Hell, and eternally leaves disbelievers there; he cites 4:40 and 21:47.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ولا يظلم ربك أحدا} أي: فيحكم بين عباده في أعمالهم جميعا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Jābir's report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Anīs, all are gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised; God settles every claim, even a slap, through good and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "يحشر الله، عز وجل الناس يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: ʿUthmān reports that the hornless sheep will exact retaliation from the horned sheep on Judgment Day; the author points to corroborating reports and his discussion of 21:47 and 6:38.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عثمان، عن عثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الجماء لتقتص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alerts Adam's descendants to Satan's enmity toward them and their father, reproaching those who ally with Iblīs and oppose their Creator and Sustainer.
rows.anchor: منبها بني آدم على عداوة إبليس لهم ولأبيهم من قبلهم، ومقرعا لمن اتبعه منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate addressed all the angels, as he had established in his discussion at the beginning of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: أي: لجميع الملائكة، كما تقدم تقريره في أول سورة "البقرة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' prostration to Adam was an act of honor, esteem, and reverence; he connects it with 15:28–29.
rows.anchor: سجود تشريف وتكريم وتعظيم، كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said angels were created from light, Iblīs from a flame of fire, and Adam from the substance already described; this supports Iblīs being from the jinn, alongside 7:12 and 38:76.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه قال: "خلقت الملائكة من نور، وخلق إبليس من مارج من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs had imitated the angels in worship and ascetic practice, so he was included in their address, but his nature betrayed him when obedience was tested.
rows.anchor: كان قد توسم بأفعال الملائكة وتشبه بهم، وتعبد وتنسك، فلهذا دخل في خطابهم

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Iblīs was never an angel, even for an instant, and is the progenitor of the jinn as Adam is of humanity; Ibn Jarīr transmits this with a sound chain.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن البصري: ما كان إبليس من الملائكة طرفة عين قط، وإنه لأصل الجن

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying Iblīs belonged to a fiery clan among the angels called jinn, was named al-Ḥārith, and kept Paradise; other jinn were created from a flame's tongue.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: كان إبليس من حي من أحياء الملائكة، يقال لهم: الجن

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying Iblīs was an eminent angelic chief with authority over the lowest heaven and earth; pride arose from this status, and God exposed it through the command to prostrate.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك أيضا، عن ابن عباس: كان إبليس من أشرف الملائكة وأكرمهم قبيلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses Iblīs being from the jinn as belonging to the keepers of Paradise, like geographic affiliations such as Meccan or Medinan; Ibn Jurayj reports a similar explanation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وقوله: {كان من الجن}

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying Iblīs was among Paradise's keepers and administered the affairs of the lowest heaven; Ibn Jarīr transmits it through al-Aʿmash, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, and Saʿīd.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: هو من خزان] (4) الجنة، وكان يدبر أمر السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says Iblīs was the chief of the angels of the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: كان رئيس ملائكة سماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Iblīs, before his disobedience, was an angel named ʿAzāzīl, an exceptionally learned and diligent inhabitant of earth from a clan called jinn; his excellence led him to arrogance.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان إبليس -قبل أن يركب المعصية-من الملائكة، اسمه عزازيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a tribe of jinn existed among the angels; Iblīs governed between heaven and earth, rebelled, and was transformed into an accursed Satan. He advises that pride-driven faults leave little hope, while one who sins may still be hoped for.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج، عن صالح مولى التوأمة وشريك بن أبي نمر، أحدهما أو كلاهما عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Iblīs belonged to the jinn-workers who worked in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أنه قال: كان من الجنانين، الذين يعملون في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many early reports about Iblīs are Israelite material to examine; some can be judged false because they contradict established truth, and the Quran suffices over earlier reports liable to alteration, additions, omissions, and fabrication.
rows.anchor: وغالبها من الإسرائيليات التي تنقل لينظر فيها، والله أعلم بحال كثير منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike earlier communities' reports, Muslim hadith scholars carefully recorded prophetic traditions and distinguished sound, fair, weak, rejected, fabricated, abandoned, and false reports and their transmitters, protecting the Prophet from lies attributed to him.
rows.anchor: الذين دونوا الحديث وحرروه، وبينوا صحيحه من حسنه، من ضعيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq means departure from God's obedience; he illustrates the usage with a date leaving its husk and a mouse emerging from its burrow to cause harm.
rows.anchor: أي: فخرج عن طاعة الله؛ فإن الفسق هو الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking Iblīs and his descendants as allies means choosing them instead of God, a wretched exchange for wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: أي: بدلا عني؛ ولهذا قال: {بئس للظالمين بدلا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the warning to Yā Sīn's account of Judgment Day, where God asks Adam's children not to worship Satan, their clear enemy, and to worship Him instead.
rows.anchor: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings taken as allies are powerless servants like humans; they neither witnessed creation nor existed then, because God alone creates, governs, and determines everything, without partner or adviser.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الذين اتخذتموهم أولياء من دوني عبيد أمثالكم، لا يملكون شيئا، ولا أشهدتهم خلقي

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik explains ʿaḍudan, “support,” to mean helpers.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: أعوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day God publicly rebukes polytheists by telling them to summon the partners they claimed in worldly life to save them; he links this to 6:94.
rows.anchor: مخبرا عما يخاطب به المشركين يوم القيامة على رؤوس الأشهاد تقريعا لهم وتوبيخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claimed partners will not respond; he links this to 28:64, 46:5–6, and 19:81–82, where the false gods become enemies of their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقال {ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and others explain mawbiqan as a place of destruction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة وغير واحد: مهلكا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Through ʿAmr al-Bakkālī, Qatāda reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that it is a deep valley separating the people of guidance from those of error on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: حدث عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: هو واد عميق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda also identifies mawbiqan as a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {موبقا} واديا في جهنم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas ibn Mālik describes it as a valley in Hell filled with pus and blood; Ibn Jarīr transmits the report.
rows.anchor: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول في قول الله تعالى: {وجعلنا بينهم موبقا} قال: واد في جهنم، من قيح ودم

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī interprets mawbiqan as enmity.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: {موبقا} : عداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent contextual meaning is destruction, though it could be a valley in Hell or another barrier: the polytheists and their claimed gods cannot reach one another, with ruin and terror between them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من السياق هاهنا: أنه المهلك، ويجوز أن يكون واديا في جهنم أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if “between them” refers to believers and disbelievers, the verse describes their separation; he connects this reading to 30:14, 30:43, 36:59, and 10:28–30.
rows.anchor: عائدا إلى المؤمنين والكافرين، كما قال عبد الله بن عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Hell is brought led by seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels, criminals know they will enter it; the dread of anticipated punishment is already a punishment.
rows.anchor: جيء بها تقاد بسبعين ألف زمام، مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals find no route to turn aside from Hell and must face it.
rows.anchor: لهم طريق يعدل بهم عنها ولا بد لهم منها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that a disbeliever sees Hell and expects to fall into it while it is still forty years' journey away; Ibn Jarīr transmits the report without a stated grading.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، عن رسول الله (3) صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "إن الكافر يرى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aḥmad's report from Abū Saʿīd adds that the disbeliever stands for fifty thousand years as though he had done no worldly work, seeing Hell forty years away.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الهيثم، عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ينصب الكافر مقدار خمسين ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained and clarified matters through varied Quranic examples to keep people from leaving guidance, yet humans argue excessively and oppose truth with falsehood, except those God guides.
rows.anchor: بينا للناس في هذا القرآن، ووضحنا لهم الأمور، وفصلناها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Prophet urged ʿAlī and Fāṭima to pray at night, ʿAlī excused them by saying their souls were in God's hand; the Prophet left and recited this verse while striking his thigh. Both Ṣaḥīḥ collections record it.
rows.anchor: أن علي بن أبي طالب أخبره، أن رسول الله (2) صلى الله عليه وسلم طرقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers across past and present reject clear truth despite signs because they demand to witness promised punishment; he links this to 26:187, 29:29, 8:32, and 15:6–7.
rows.anchor: وأنه ما منعهم من اتباع ذلك إلا طلبهم أن يشاهدوا العذاب الذي وعدوا به عيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent of earlier peoples is that they were overtaken and destroyed collectively; alternatively, the coming punishment will be seen directly, face to face.
rows.anchor: من غشيانهم بالعذاب وأخذهم عن آخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers come only with good news for believers and warnings for those who reject them, before punishment arrives.
rows.anchor: قبل العذاب مبشرين (6) من صدقهم وآمن بهم، ومنذرين (7) من كذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers use false arguments to weaken the truth brought by the messengers, but their attempt cannot succeed.
rows.anchor: {ليدحضوا به} أي: ليضعفوا به {الحق} الذي جاءتهم به الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mock God's proofs, miraculous signs, and the warnings of punishment, which is an especially severe form of denial.
rows.anchor: {واتخذوا آياتي وما أنذروا هزوا} أي: اتخذوا الحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is more unjust than one reminded by God's signs who turns away, ignores them, and forgets the evil deeds he has sent ahead.
rows.anchor: فأعرض عنها، أي: تناساها وأعرض عنها، ولم يصغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's coverings on their hearts prevent understanding the Quran and its clarification, while their ears bear a spiritual deafness to guidance; they will never be guided if called.
rows.anchor: {أكنة} أي: أغطية وغشاوة، {أن يفقهوه} أي: لئلا يفهموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving and merciful; if He seized people for their deeds He would hasten punishment, as in 35:45 and 13:6.
rows.anchor: كما قال: {ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God patiently covers and forgives, and may guide some from error; those who persist have an appointed day from which there is no escape or turning aside.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر أنه يحلم ويستر ويغفر، وربما هدى بعضهم من الغي إلى الرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed earlier peoples for disbelief and stubbornness at a fixed, known time that neither advances nor recedes, warning the current polytheists that they are no more honored than those peoples and should fear the punishment.
rows.anchor: الأمم السالفة والقرون الخالية أهلكناهم بسبب كفرهم وعنادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' journey began after he learned of a servant at the junction of two seas who knew what Moses did not; he tells his attendant Joshua ibn Nūn that he will keep travelling until they arrive, even if it takes a long age.
rows.anchor: أنه ذكر له أن عبدا من عباد الله بمجمع البحرين، عنده من العلم ما لم يحط به موسى

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: The poet al-Farazdaq's line illustrates the usage of lā abraḥ as continuing or not ceasing until a destination is reached.
rows.anchor: قال الفرزدق: فما برحوا حتى تهادت نساؤهم

rows.speaker: قتادة وغير واحد
rows.claim: Qatāda and others locate the two seas as the Persian Sea to the east and the Roman Sea to the west.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وغير واحد: وهما بحر فارس مما يلي المشرق، وبحر الروم مما يلي المغرب

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī places the junction at Tangier, in the far west; the author leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: مجمع البحرين عند طنجة، يعني في أقصى بلاد المغرب، فالله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuqban means a long span, even if Moses were to travel for ages; Ibn Jarīr cites Arab usage in Qays as a year.
rows.anchor: أي: ولو أني أسير حقبا من الزمان

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr defines ḥuqban as eighty years.
rows.anchor: ثم قد روي عن عبد الله بن عمرو أنه قال: الحقب ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid defines ḥuqban as seventy autumns.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سبعون خريفا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Ibn Zayd understand ḥuqban to mean a long time or age.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: {أو أمضي حقبا} قال: دهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses carried a salted fish and was told its disappearance would mark the destination; while they slept at the junction, water from the spring of life revived it, and it leapt from Joshua's basket into the sea, leaving a tunnel-like path that stayed open.
rows.anchor: أنه كان قد أمر بحمل حوت مملوح معه، وقيل له: متى فقدت الحوت فهو ثمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the fish's trace became like stone.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: صار أثره كأنه حجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-ʿAwfī reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying the fish dried the sea wherever it touched, leaving stone behind.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: جعل الحوت لا يمس شيئا من البحر إلا يبس حتى يكون صخرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's report through Ibn ʿAbbās, the Prophet says the water opened only at the fish's place, like a window, so Moses later saw its passage.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ذكر حديث ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the fish made a tunnel across land to the sea, then moved through it, and the water froze wherever it travelled.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: سرب من البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two are both said to have forgotten the fish although Joshua alone forgot it, like the statement that pearls and coral emerge from both seas when one view says they emerge from the salt sea alone; he cites 55:22.
rows.anchor: ونسب النسيان إليهما وإن كان يوشع هو الذي نسيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After passing the spot by one stage, Moses asks for lunch and says the journey has caused fatigue; naṣaban means tiredness.
rows.anchor: أي: الذي جاوزا فيه المكان {نصبا} يعني: تعبا.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that Ibn Masʿūd read the clause with the order changed: Satan made me forget to mention the fish.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: ["وما أنسانيه أن أذكره إلا الشيطان]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and his attendant retrace their steps and follow the trail of their own walking; qaṣaṣan means tracing the track.
rows.anchor: أي: رجعا {على آثارهما} أي: طريقهما {قصصا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls Nauf al-Bikālī an enemy of God and rejects his claim that Moses' companion of al-Khiḍr was not the Moses of the Israelites; the sound prophetic report identifies them as the same Moses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كذب عدو الله، حدثنا أبي بن كعب، رضي الله عنه، أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet relates that Moses claimed to be the most knowledgeable, was reproved for not referring knowledge to God, then learned of a more knowledgeable servant and received the fish sign for finding him.
rows.anchor: إن موسى قام خطيبا في بني إسرائيل فسئل: أي الناس أعلم؟ قال: أنا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report says Moses travelled with Joshua and the fish; the fish revived and entered the sea at the rock while God held the current like an arch, and Joshua forgot to tell Moses.
rows.anchor: فخرج منه، فسقط في البحر واتخذ (9) سبيله في البحر سربا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Moses felt fatigue only after passing the appointed place; Joshua then recalled the fish and its extraordinary route through the sea.
rows.anchor: ولم يجد موسى النصب حتى جاوزا المكان الذي أمره الله به

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After retracing their path, Moses found al-Khiḍr covered in a garment; al-Khiḍr questioned his greeting, recognized Moses of Israel, and heard his request to be taught rightly guided knowledge.
rows.anchor: فإذا رجل مسجى بثوب، فسلم عليه موسى، فقال الخضر: وأنى بأرضك السلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr explains that each has knowledge God taught him which the other lacks; Moses promises patience by God's will, and al-Khiḍr instructs him not to ask until given an explanation.
rows.anchor: إني على علم من علم الله علمنيه، لا تعلمه أنت، وأنت على علم من علم الله علمكه الله لا أعلمه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: People who recognized al-Khiḍr carried Moses and him on a ship without fare; al-Khiḍr removed a plank, and Moses objected that this could drown its passengers, then asked pardon for his forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: فعرفوا الخضر، فحملوهم (2) بغير نول، فلما ركبا في السفينة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies the ship incident as Moses' first lapse, due to forgetfulness; a bird's sip from the sea illustrates how little Moses' and al-Khiḍr's knowledge is beside God's.
rows.anchor: كانت الأولى من موسى نسيانا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Khiḍr kills a boy whom Moses protests was innocent; al-Khiḍr calls this harder to bear, and Moses promises to stop accompanying him if he asks again.
rows.anchor: فأخذ الخضر رأسه [بيده] (7) فاقتلعه بيده فقتله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After the inhospitable village refuses them food or lodging, al-Khiḍr straightens a collapsing wall; Moses suggests taking payment, and al-Khiḍr declares their separation and promises an explanation.
rows.anchor: فقال موسى: قوم أتيناهم فلم يطعمونا ولم يضيفونا، {لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet wished Moses had remained patient so God could have told more of the two men's story.
rows.anchor: وددنا أن موسى كان صبر حتى يقص الله علينا من خبرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Ibn ʿAbbās read the ship verse with “behind them” and “every sound ship,” rather than the common wording.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كان ابن عباس يقرأ: "وكان أمامهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة صالحة غصبا"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr also reports Ibn ʿAbbās reading that the boy was a disbeliever while his parents were believers.
rows.anchor: وكان يقرأ: "وأما الغلام فكان كافرا وكان أبواه مؤمنين"

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: A second Bukhārī version says a spring of life stood at the rock and revived the fish; it also expands the bird analogy to all creatures' knowledge compared with God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفي أصل الصخرة عين يقال لها: الحياة، لا يصيب من مائها شيء إلا حيي
